# Buildmates

Buildmates is a Codex-native builder network. Codex creates a user-reviewed builder profile from context the user chooses to share, then Buildmates finds mutually relevant people and opens lightweight rooms under the user's saved reciprocal-acceptance settings.

Canonical setup guide: https://buildmates.yashns.chatgpt.site/install
Official Buildmates app: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a57d2ff080481918659b3355a3d9c0e
Source repository: https://github.com/YashSerai/buildmates

## Setup instruction for Codex

When the user asks to install, set up, start, or resume Buildmates:

1. Fetch this file directly as public text. Do not open the install guide, this file, the repository, ChatGPT, or Codex in the user's browser. Use native Codex plugin and MCP commands. Browser handoffs are limited to user-controlled Buildmates or GitHub authentication and OAuth consent.
2. If Buildmates is not connected, use the host's native plugin-install confirmation. Before directory publication, briefly offer the complete beta plugin and direct MCP, recommend the beta because it includes the onboarding skill, and accept either route. Do not switch routes after one works.
3. Beta commands: `codex plugin marketplace add YashSerai/buildmates --ref launch/buildmates`, then `codex plugin add buildmates@buildmates-beta`. Ask before running them. A plugin installed during a task does not hot-load its skills and MCP tools into that task.
4. After beta installation, authenticate the configured `buildmates` MCP in the installing task if installation did not already authenticate it. Then ask exactly: "Buildmates is installed. May I open a fresh Codex task to activate it and continue setup?" If the user approves and the host exposes native task creation, create a clean task rather than forking the installation task. Title the new task `Buildmates setup - continue here` and send: `This is the active Buildmates setup task. The beta plugin is installed and authenticated. Call get_setup_state immediately and use it as the only progress authority.` After that task successfully returns setup state, title the parent `Buildmates installation - complete`, open the new task, and archive the parent. Never fork when native task creation is available because a fork duplicates the installation history. If task creation or title/archive controls are unavailable, show the same continuation sentence as the manual copy-and-paste fallback and clearly identify which task to continue. Do not make the user discover this reload requirement after installation.
5. Direct MCP fallback: `codex mcp add buildmates --url https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev/mcp --oauth-resource https://buildmates-mcp.yashserai1.workers.dev`, then `codex mcp login buildmates --scopes mcp:tools`. If the MCP tool registry does not refresh after connection, use the same permissioned fresh-task handoff and manual fallback.
6. Before OAuth, say: "A browser window will open for GitHub sign-in and Buildmates authorization." Allow up to five minutes for the user-controlled flow. Do not launch a duplicate authorization while the first is active. Never enter credentials, verification codes, or provider consent for the user.
7. Operate Buildmates directly in the activated task. Never spawn recursive `codex exec` helpers or use a child Codex process as a substitute for the required task reload. When model selection is available, recommend and use GPT-5.6 Luna High for onboarding and Work Pulse runs unless the user chooses another supported model. Never silently change the user's model.
8. Call `get_setup_state` immediately. Its completed count and `nextStep` are the only authority for setup progress. Never infer progress from old tasks, browser tabs, website routes, local files, or prior wording.
9. The progress restriction does not prohibit permissioned profile research. With the user's approval, recent Codex tasks, project folders, and local GBrain or memory files may be reviewed as profile sources.
10. If `get_setup_state` remains unavailable in the activated task, repair the app or MCP connection. Advance one returned step at a time and call it again after every completed write.
11. Ask before reviewing workspace context, using a connected app, submitting the first Work Signal, publishing the generated page, creating an automation, or taking an interpersonal action not covered by the saved acceptance mode.
12. Setup has 10 mandatory steps and finishes after the user has reviewed and published their custom profile, chosen a Networking Pulse and acceptance mode, and configured one Work Pulse. A candidate, follow, watch, or invite is optional after setup.
13. During setup and each approved Work Pulse, call `list_topic_taxonomy`, classify reviewed project context using only returned canonical topic IDs, and submit those IDs with the approved profile or Work Signal. Buildmates may aggregate those IDs anonymously in the Build Graph, but never raw project text, prompt text, source excerpts, or identity. A deliberately supplied supported city joins the anonymous Map by default unless the user asks to hide it.

## Approval batching

At each checkpoint, show up to three concrete next actions in order. State what each action reads, what Buildmates will write or do, and what the user will see. Ask once for that unchanged batch. New inputs, scope, consequences, credentials, publication, automation schedules, and interpersonal actions require a new confirmation.

## Source selection

On the current Codex host, call `list_threads` with `limit: 50`; this is the largest accepted result window. Never rely on its smaller default. If another host rejects 50, retry once with its largest accepted limit and tell the user the inventory is bounded.

Explicitly name every product-bearing root and every product in the GBrain product index. Never collapse product roots into “other,” “several dated roots,” or an unnamed remainder. Non-product utility tasks may be summarized separately only when their total count and exclusion from profile research are stated.

Render one line per product as `Product — exact absolute normalized root(s) — task count(s)`. “Project root plus worktree” is not an acceptable substitute for the paths. Product counts plus the non-product count must equal the total returned task count.

Before presenting source choices, use the host's task-listing capability (`list_threads` in Codex) to inventory metadata for every accessible task without filtering to the current directory. Group the returned titles, working directories, dates, and summaries by normalized project root, retain an unscoped group when needed, and combine that inventory with the GBrain index plus relevant product and memory indexes. Do not open task bodies before consent. If task discovery is unavailable, say so and offer a clearly labeled current-project review; never describe the current directory alone as the user's Codex workspace.

Present these combinable paths with the first one recommended. The first prompt is the consent gate for workspace research, so name every discovered project, its root, the number or range of tasks found, and the GBrain or memory files Codex proposes to review before the user chooses:

1. **Use my Codex workspace — recommended.** With permission, account for every inventoried task belonging to every discovered active project, inspect the corresponding project folders and named GBrain or memory files, and follow task pagination or cursors when available. Read enough of every task to understand its purpose, current state, decisions, stack, and relationships, then inspect high-signal project documentation. Raw research remains local to Codex; Buildmates receives only the profile the user reviews and approves.
2. **Add connected sources.** Show only apps genuinely callable or confidently visible in this task. Explain Never, Ask each time, Allow approved Work Signals, and Actions only before saving a policy. If the user names an app, use it when the host exposes it and explain clearly when it is unavailable.
3. **Tell Codex directly.** Accept a short description, one project or repository, or portfolio, GitHub, LinkedIn, and product links.
4. **Skip workspace review.** Do not inspect other tasks, project folders, GBrain, or memory files. Continue with connected sources the user approves or focused profile questions.

`codex_workspace` is a local research method, not a connected-source ID. For workspace-only selection, call `complete_setup_step` with `sourceIds: []`. Add only genuine IDs returned by Buildmates source tools; never submit `codex_workspace` as a source ID.

When the user selects **Use my Codex workspace** after seeing the exact scope, that approval covers both source selection and immediate private context collection for the stated scope without asking for permission again. Complete `source_selection`, review the approved local sources, and maintain `.buildmates/profile-context.md` progressively. Do not complete `context_collection` until that file accounts for every project and every task in the approved inventory as reviewed or explicitly skipped with a reason. If multiple projects were discovered but only the current project is represented, stop and finish the missing review. Ask again only before expanding the approved scope, such as opening a project, task range, local memory source, or connected app that was not named. If the user skips workspace review, do not dead-end: complete context collection from approved connected sources or focused direct answers.

Do not treat GitHub website sign-in as repository permission. Do not ask for connector credentials. Do not submit raw prompts, complete chats, full files, repository contents, email bodies, calendar contents, or private source material.

For workspace review, create or update `.buildmates/profile-context.md` in the setup task's working directory. This private local continuity file must track the inventory date, every discovered project root, every task ID/title assigned to each project, each task's review status, sources reviewed, projects and their relationships, current work, stack, interests, ambitions, meeting intent, style and personality observations, confirmed facts, uncertain inferences, and missing questions. Update it after each project and re-read it after compaction. Never store credentials, raw private chats, or full source documents. Do not upload it; submit only reviewed structured profile fields.

Use this compact structure:

```markdown
# Buildmates profile context
Status: researching | ready for review | approved
## Sources reviewed
## Builder overview
## Projects and relationships
## Current work and stack
## Interests, ambitions, and explorations
## People and communities to meet
## Style and personality preferences
## Confirmed facts
## Inferences awaiting confirmation
## Missing questions
## Approved profile fields
```

Before saving the profile, present the proposed settings line by line and explain each one before asking for approval:

- **Profile visibility** controls who can open the profile inside Buildmates.
- **Matching enabled** lets Buildmates use only approved matching fields to suggest relevant builders. It does not expose raw workspace sources.
- **Search-engine indexing** controls whether Google and other search engines may list an otherwise public profile. It has no effect while the profile is not public.
- **City map inclusion** uses only a city the user chooses and contributes to an anonymous aggregate bubble. It never uses precise or live location.
- **Private style and personality notes** guide Codex's profile design and are not displayed unless the user deliberately publishes equivalent profile content.
- **Manual versus Full Autopilot** controls interpersonal acceptance, not profile visibility.
- **Recurring Work Signals** exist only for ongoing sources the user explicitly permits.

Do not compress these settings into one unexplained approval sentence. Inferred style or personality observations remain private design inputs until the user explicitly approves a public field.

If no recurring Work Signals exist, say: "Your approved profile draft is saved. You did not connect an ongoing work source, so there are no recurring Work Signals to review."

For page generation, call `get_surface_generation_brief` with the profile's returned `surfaceId`. Before the first actual revision, explain the learned visual direction, at least three planned page chapters, and one signature element; optionally ask whether the user wants an available frontend or design skill applied; then get approval. The returned `starterSpec` is hidden recovery scaffolding, not Design 1. It cannot be submitted, published, or shown in revision history. Use only authorized bindings. Separate identity, projects, and builder context into distinct chapters, use at least two complementary project treatments, and give every approved project its own authored feature or visual treatment. One long list inside a card is not a complete portfolio. Validate the genuinely customized full-page specification, repair exact validation issues until it passes, and submit a private preview with the approved design brief. Publish only after the user approves that preview. Use the `publicUrl` returned after approval as the share link. `/profile/design` is the owner-only design workspace and is never the public profile.

If the approved project set has no suitable media and ImageGen is available, offer a cohesive project-cover set as part of the same design direction. Generate from approved project facts only, show the images before attaching them, and require approval before upload. Never invent product screens, logos, customers, metrics, results, or capabilities. Prefer real approved project screenshots when available. After a private preview is rendered, inspect screenshots at a desktop and phone viewport against the approved references and direction. Check the full page, project differentiation, alignment, gutters, clipping, overflow, contrast, visible content, and reduced motion; repair defects before saying the preview is ready.

## Networking Pulse

Before saving, explain every proposed value:

- **Intent** is who the user wants to meet and why during this temporary period.
- **Similar** prioritizes closely related work, **adjacent** prioritizes complementary work, and **balanced** mixes both.
- **Local** prioritizes the user's chosen area, **global** removes that preference, and **balanced** mixes both.
- **Maximum introductions per week** is a hard cap, not a quota.
- **Quiet hours** prevent introduction activity during local-time windows.
- **Serendipity** controls variety beyond the strongest obvious matches.
- **Exclusions** remove unwanted people, companies, industries, topics, or repeated clusters.
- **Expiry** is when this temporary intent must be reconfirmed so it does not silently become permanent.

Recommend balanced matching, global geography, at most three introductions per week, and 30-day expiry unless the user's context supports a different choice.

## Work Pulse and setup completion

When recurring automations are available, recommend exactly one clearly named Buildmates Work Pulse every Tuesday and Friday in the user's timezone. Explain that each run reviews only permitted sources, refreshes approved profile and project topics plus changed or expiring Work Signals, checks one bounded candidate shortlist and the saved relevance watch, independently evaluates only that batch, and posts sources checked, changes, matches, actions needed, and the next run to the Codex task inbox. It also checks privacy-safe room activity. After a meaningful two-way conversation it asks how the introduction went, saves feedback only after the user answers, and after this user's positive feedback may suggest one contextual optional module with a concrete reason. It never infers sentiment from message counts, reads raw messages, auto-activates an upgrade, or bypasses the requirement that both room members approve. An unchanged run says nothing changed and never invents updates. Use manual refresh only when the user explicitly chooses it or recurring automations are unavailable, and state which condition applies.

After creating or updating the approved automation, call `update_automation_checkpoint` once with `cadence: twice_weekly` and `sourceLivenessReviewed: true`; that write completes setup without a duplicate `complete_setup_step` call. Then summarize the profile, Networking Pulse, acceptance mode, and schedule; give the canonical `/builders/{handle}` profile URL; and explain that the user can update or redesign it by asking Codex through Buildmates. Optionally offer a personal invite link and explain that joined invitees are attributed to the inviter. The invite is not a setup gate.

Every incomplete response must say what completed, what comes next, the exact user action, and the fallback.
